title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + tool schema mapping + stable streaming for tool messages
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer to fully support OpenAI-style function/tool calling semantics (including the newer `tool_choice` return path), map OpenAI function schemas to Redwood's tool schema, and ensure tool-related messages stream stably to clients. This PR implements schema translation, resolves ambiguous tool selection semantics, and stabilizes streaming of tool invocation and tool-result messages so downstream SDKs and clients receive a consistent event sequence.

Summary of changes: implemented an OpenAI->Redwood function schema mapper that translates types/params/required fields to Redwood tool descriptors; added a tool_choice resolution step that prefers exact name matches, then aliases, then best-effort fuzzy match with a configurable policy; introduced a streaming envelope for tool messages (event types: tool.invoke.start, tool.invoke.chunk, tool.invoke.end, tool.result) to avoid mixed payload chunking; added feature-flag gated behavior to preserve previous behavior for older clients.

Compatibility: The default behavior preserves existing Redwood tool invocation semantics but enables a compat mode when an OpenAI-compatible request is detected (messages.role=="tool" or schema present). Tool schema mapping aims to be lossless for common OpenAI function constructs; unsupported schema features are surfaced to logs and converted to a generic object param.

Testing & rollout: comprehensive unit tests for schema mapping edge cases, integration tests for streaming sequences, and an e2e smoke against openai-compat example app. Rollout is feature-flagged and can be toggled per-customer; will enable for internal canary orgs first.

Checklist:
- [x] Schema mapper implementation (src/openai_compat/schema_mapper)
- [x] tool_choice resolver and aliasing (src/openai_compat/tool_choice)
- [x] Streaming envelope for tool messages (src/openai_compat/streaming)
- [x] Backwards-compatible feature flag (config/openai_compat.yaml)
- [x] Unit/integration tests (tests/compat/test_tool_mapping.py, tests/compat/test_streaming_tools.py)
- [x] Docs updates (redwood-docs/content/openai-compat/tool-calling.md)

References: Linear ENG-4187, ENG-4250; related PRs pr-19734 and pr-21342 for earlier tool-calling work.

review_comments: Ethan Chen: Can we guarantee deterministic tool_choice when names overlap across tool namespaces? Suggest adding explicit namespace resolution and log if fuzzy match used.
Sofia Patel: Responded - added namespace-aware resolution and a warning telemetry event when fuzzy fallback is used. Policy is configurable via config/openai_compat.yaml.
Liam O'Connor: Streaming envelope looks good; however ensure backward compatibility for older SDKs that expect raw tool messages. Suggest feature flag + header-based detection.
Sofia Patel: Responded - implemented feature flag and header detection (OpenAI-Compat: 1) with a fallback to legacy streaming for older clients.
Priya Gupta: +1 after tests added for large streaming payloads and chunk ordering. Verified ordering by sequence ids in events.
release_notes: Adds OpenAI function->Redwood tool schema mapping, deterministic tool_choice resolution with aliasing and configurable fuzzy fallback, and stable streaming envelope for tool invocation/results. Feature-flagged and rolled out behind canary. Backwards-compatible by default.
